hypothesis: Dispatching high-cost route candidates first improves worker utilization versus FIFO queue order.
settings: CIXG1 BEST, 65,536-byte blocks, 5,616 candidates, four leased physical CPUs, 2 GiB process memory cap, no swap; only dispatch order changed from preceding PPM-order search.
interpretation: The first prioritized run was faster, the replicate was slower. Two prioritized measurements average 325.67 seconds, only 0.7% below the single FIFO control; this does not establish a speedup. Both produced byte-identical archives. Frozen Python cross-decoding was already verified on this exact archive SHA in the preceding PPM-order trial.
decision: Do not promote cost-priority scheduling. Restore FIFO candidate dispatch; retain four-worker dynamic candidate execution.
